If you have any question about matters on the agenda, or requests for assistance, please contact the Community Development

 AGENDA  2
REGULAR MEETING OF THE PLANNING COMMISSION
Wednesday, March 6, 2019

  7. PLANNING COMMISSION ITEMS

  OLD BUSINESS

  (1)  GLENDALE MUNICIPAL CODE AMENDMENT CASE NO. PZC1823357
  (CONTINUED FROM FEBRUARY 6, 2019)
  LOCATION:  CITYWIDE
  APPLICANT:  CITY OF GLENDALE
  STAFF:  Jay Platt – Senior Urban Designer
  PROJECT DESCRIPTION
  It is proposed to amend Titles 2,15, and 30 of the Glendale Municipal Code, 1995, relating
  generally to deterring the unpermitted demolition of historic resources and contributing
  buildings in historic districts, and including minor changes and clarifications of other code
  sections. (Code Amendment Case No. PZC1823357).

  ENVIRONMENTAL DETERMINATION
  The project is exempt from CEQA review under a categorical exemption because the
  ordinance will enhance the protection of historic buildings through the improvement of
  the City’s enforcement policies in cases of illegal, unpermitted demolition as a Class 8
  (“Actions by Regulatory Agencies for Protection of the Environment”) exemption
  pursuant to Section 15308 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  REQUESTED ACTION
  The Community Development Department staff recommends that the Planning
  Commission review the proposed amendments to Titles 2, 15, and 30 and recommend that
  the City Council adopt the proposed amendments, and as stated in the staff report dated
  March 6, 2019.

  NEW BUSINESS

  (2) LOCATION:  CITY WIDE
  APPLICANT:  CITY OF GLENDALE
  STAFF:  Laura Stotler
   Ordinance to establish standards, procedures and fees
  for home-sharing activities and to prohibit vacation rentals
  (SHORT-TERM RENTAL ORDINANCE)
  PROJECT DESCRIPTION
  Amendments to the Glendale Municipal Code (Title 5 and Title 30) to establish standards,
  procedures and fees for home-sharing activities and to prohibit vacation rentals in the City
  of Glendale known as the Short-term Rental Ordinance. This ordinance has been
  prepared following direction of the City Council on October 2, 2018.
 AGENDA  3
REGULAR MEETING OF THE PLANNING COMMISSION
Wednesday, March 6, 2019

  The Short-term Rental Ordinance is exempt from the California Environmental Quality Act
  under Class 1 Existing Facilities (Title 14 of the California Code of Regulations, Section
  15301); (1) because it consists of permitting short-term residential uses in existing
  residential units, with negligible expansion of the use; (2) it can be seen with certainty that
  there is no possibility that the activity in question may have a significant effect on the
  environment because the use already exists and are only being further restricted (Title 14
  of the California Code of Regulations, Section 15061(b) (3); and, (3) adoption of this
  ordinance is exempt from the requirements of CEQA because it constitutes a governmental
  fiscal activity that does not involve any commitment to any specific project which may result
  in a potentially significant physical impact of the environment (Title 14 of the California
  Code of Regulations, Section 15378(b) (4).
  REQUESTED ACTION
  The Community Development Department staff recommends that the Planning
  Commission continue this item to their regular Planning Commission hearing of
  May 1, 2019.

  8. COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT DEPARTMENT UPDATES

  9. COMMENTS FROM COMMISSIONERS

 10. ADJOURNMENT

  PROJECT DESCRIPTION
  It is proposed to amend Titles 2, 15, and 30 of the Glendale Municipal Code, 1995,
  relating generally to deterring the unpermitted demolition of historic resources and
  contributing buildings in historic districts, and including minor changes and
  clarifications of other code sections. (Code Amendment Case No. PZC1823357).

  ENVIRONMENTAL DETERMINATION
  The project is exempt from CEQA review under a categorical exemption because
  the ordinance will enhance the protection of historic buildings through the

  2
 Planning Comm ission Minutes
March 6, 20 19

  STAFF
  Staff Member Jay Platt, Senior Urban Designer, presented the staff report and
  highlighted the main items of the staff report. He answered questions from the
  Planning Commissioners.

  Mr. Platt gave a Powerpoint presentation detailing all the key points of the staff
  report.

  Mr. Platt informed the Planning Commissioners that City Council directed Planning
  Division staff to study ways to enhance the City's ability to deter illegal demolition
  of designated or potential historic resources and contributing properties in
  designated or pending historic districts and punish those responsible for the loss.
  Current Glendale regulations give the City the ability to enforce criminal and civil
  penalties against property owners or others who demolish a designated historic
  resource without a demolition permit.

  Mr. Platt stated that Community Development Department staff recommends that
  the Planning Commission review the proposed amendments to Titles 2, 15, and 30
  of G.M.C. , and recommend that the City Council adopt the proposed amendments,
  and as stated in the staff report dated March 6, 2019.

  APPLICANT
  City of Glendale - Presentation by staff.

  WRITTEN COMMUNICATION
  In Support:  None.
  Interested Persons: None
  In Opposition:  None.

  SPEAKING AT THE HEARING

  In Support
  - C. Jurca

  In Opposition:  No one.
  Interested Persons: No one.

  DISCUSSION BY COMMISSIONERS

  Upon questioning by the Planning Commissioners, Mr. Platt stated that:
  -- A demolition clearance is required prior to the issuance of a 'Demolition Permit'.

  3
 Planning Conunission Minutes
March 6, 2019

  -- Goal of the Code Amendment is to deter illegal demolition of properties in the City's
  designated and pending historic districts.
  -- Owner of the property is responsible to apply for National Register of Historic
  Resources.
  -- Historic Preservation Commission was very supportive of the code amendment
  regarding demolition deterrence and made some recommendations.
  -- It was presented to Design Review Board.
  -- If a property is thirty (30) years old or less, a demolition clearance can be obtained,
  without an environmental review

  Planning Commissioners discussed the following :
  Noncontributing houses and new houses.
  Section No. 15.20.030 - Authority was discussed in details.
  Property owners to be notified that their properties have been designated
  historic property by the City.
  Appeals
  CEQA
  Mills Act Tax Reduction
  National Historic Register
  Partial demolition
  Educating the public

  Planning Commissioners made the following motion.

  MOTION
  Moved by Planning Commissioner Chraghchian, seconded by Planning
  Commissioner Astorian, that this project will enhance the protection of historic
  buildings through the improvement of the City's enforcement policies in cases of
  illegal, unpermitted demolition, as well as clarify and correct other portions of the
  Municipal Code relating to historic preservation, that the project is exempt from CEQA
  as a Class 5 ("Minor Alterations in Land Use Limitations") and as a Class 8 ("Actions
  by Regulatory Agencies for Protection of the Environment") categorical exemptions
  pursuant to Sections 15305 and 15308 of the State CEQA Guidelines, and that upon
  consideration of the proposed ordinance at a public hearing the Planning Commission
  hereby recommends that the City Council adopt the proposed amendments to Titles
  2, 15, and 30 of the Glendale Municipal Code, 1995, subject to all comments and
  recommendations discussed at the hearing on the matter.

  Adopted this 5 th day of March, 2019.

  VOTE
  Ayes :  Astorian , Chraghchian, Lee, Shahbazian
  Noes:  None
  Absent:  None
  Abstain:  None
